--parallel.label: Parallel slots
--parallel.why: Splits the configured context N ways rather than multiplying it — n_ctx 131072 with --parallel 2 gives each request only 65536 usable tokens. Use 1 for a config meant to serve one long conversation at its full context; more only for short requests served concurrently.

--ctx-checkpoints.label: Context checkpoints
--ctx-checkpoints.why: Lets the engine restore a saved KV-cache checkpoint instead of reprocessing a whole conversation from scratch. Upstream llama.cpp has had hang bugs in this code path, so test a model before relying on it; 0 turns it off.

--cache-type-k.label: KV cache quant (K)
--cache-type-k.why: Quantizes the attention key cache to shrink its memory footprint at some quality cost. It can differ from --cache-type-v (e.g. q4_0/q8_0).

--cache-type-v.label: KV cache quant (V)
--cache-type-v.why: Quantizes the attention value cache. Paired with --cache-type-k; see that entry.

--flash-attn.label: Flash attention
--flash-attn.why: Enables the fused flash-attention kernel — faster and lower-memory attention on supported backends. Normally safe to leave on.

--jinja.label: Jinja chat template
--jinja.why: Uses the model's own Jinja chat template (from the GGUF metadata) instead of llama.cpp's built-in template guesser. Needed for any model whose prompt format the built-in guesser doesn't already know.

--mmproj.label: Multimodal projector
--mmproj.why: Path to the vision/multimodal projector weights, required for any model that accepts image input. Set automatically from the config's linked mmproj artifact, not typed by hand.

--load-mode.label: Model load mode
--load-mode.why: How the weight file is loaded: "none" reads it all into memory up front (what --no-mmap used to do), "mmap" memory-maps it on demand, "mlock" / "mmap+mlock" also pin it in RAM, "auto" lets llama.cpp choose (mmap unless a device can't). Replaces --mmap / --no-mmap / --mlock / --direct-io, which current upstream builds reject.

--no-mmap.label: Disable mmap (deprecated)
--no-mmap.why: Forces the whole weight file to be read into memory up front instead of memory-mapped on demand. Slower to start, but avoids page-fault stalls mid-generation on some filesystem/GPU-driver combinations. Deprecated: upstream removed it (ggml-org/llama.cpp #28334) — builds from the 2026-10 rebase reject it; use --load-mode none instead. Older builds still accept both.

--threads.label: CPU threads
--threads.why: CPU thread count for the parts of inference that aren't offloaded to the GPU (tokenization, sampling, any CPU-resident layers). Rarely the bottleneck when the whole model is on the GPU.

--swa-full.label: Full sliding-window attention cache
--swa-full.why: Keeps the full sliding-window attention cache resident rather than the reduced form — needed by some hybrid/recurrent architectures to reuse the cache across turns. It interacts with --ctx-checkpoints, so test the model before changing either.

--spec-type.label: Speculative decoding
--spec-type.why: Selects the speculative-decoding strategy (e.g. a draft model or MTP head) used to predict several tokens ahead and verify them in a batch — a real throughput win when the draft's acceptance rate is high, and a real slowdown when it isn't.

--spec-draft-model.label: Draft model
--spec-draft-model.why: Path to the smaller draft model used for speculative decoding, typed by hand (unlike --mmproj there is no catalog-linked draft-model artifact). Some drafting methods need no separate file.

--spec-draft-n-max.label: Max draft tokens
--spec-draft-n-max.why: Upper bound on how many tokens the draft model predicts ahead before the main model verifies them in one batch. Larger values raise the potential speedup but also the cost of a rejected batch.

--model-draft.label: Draft model
--model-draft.why: Short-flag form of the draft-model path (-md): the same role as --spec-draft-model, used by some speculative-decoding methods. Typed by hand, not catalog-linked.

--n-gpu-layers.label: GPU-offloaded layers
--n-gpu-layers.why: Number of transformer layers placed on the GPU rather than the CPU. 999 means all of them — llama.cpp clamps to the model's real layer count. Lowering it trades inference speed for less GPU memory pressure.

--batch-size.label: Prompt batch size
--batch-size.why: Logical batch size for prompt (prefill) processing. Larger values process a prompt faster at the cost of a bigger compute buffer; usually tuned together with --ubatch-size.

--ubatch-size.label: Physical batch size
--ubatch-size.why: The physical (GPU-kernel) batch size within each logical batch (--batch-size). Must be ≤ --batch-size; tune the two together for the hardware.

--reasoning-budget.label: Reasoning token budget
--reasoning-budget.why: Caps how many tokens a reasoning model may spend inside its <think> block before it's forced to produce a final answer. Prevents a model from burning its whole context on internal reasoning and never answering.

--chat-template-kwargs.label: Chat template kwargs
--chat-template-kwargs.why: Extra JSON arguments passed into the Jinja chat template, for example {"preserve_thinking":true}. The names and the right value depend on the model's template; a wrong value can look like a reasoning-budget or template bug (for example all thinking and an empty answer).

--chat-template-file.label: Chat template override
--chat-template-file.why: Replaces the GGUF's embedded chat template with an external file, for a model whose embedded template is broken or missing something it needs.

--repeat-penalty.label: Repeat penalty
--repeat-penalty.why: Penalizes tokens the model has generated recently. llama-server's default (1.0) is effectively off, which lets some reasoning-heavy models fall into repetition loops — a sampling issue, not a template one.

--dry-multiplier.label: DRY sampler strength
--dry-multiplier.why: Strength of the DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) repetition-breaking sampler, off by default (0.0). Often used with --repeat-penalty; removing it from a model that needs it can bring repetition loops back.

--temp.label: Sampling temperature
--temp.why: Standard sampling temperature. If a config pairs it with repetition controls, change them together: altering the temperature alone can bring repetition loops back.

--trust-remote-code.label: Trust remote code
--trust-remote-code.why: Allows vLLM to execute custom modeling code shipped in the model repo rather than only vLLM's built-in architectures. Required for models vLLM doesn't natively recognize.

--dtype.label: Weight dtype
--dtype.why: The compute/storage dtype vLLM loads weights as (e.g. bfloat16). Distinct from a GGUF quantization scheme.

--tensor-parallel-size.label: Tensor-parallel size
--tensor-parallel-size.why: Number of GPUs to shard each layer's weights across. 1 on a single-GPU machine.

--gpu-memory-utilization.label: GPU memory utilization
--gpu-memory-utilization.why: Fraction of GPU memory vLLM is allowed to reserve for weights + KV cache (0.98 = nearly all of it). Lowering this leaves memory for other processes but shrinks the usable KV cache.

hazards.parallel: Context is split, not multiplied: n_ctx {{nCtx}} with {{flag}} {{n}} gives each request only {{perSlot}} usable tokens. Verify this is intentional (a deliberate concurrent-short-request tradeoff) rather than a leftover default.
hazards.ctx_checkpoints: Upstream llama.cpp has had hang bugs in this code path. Check that this is intentional before relying on it for a long-running conversation.

--tp.label: Tensor-parallel ranks
--tp.why: How many GPU ranks Radiance shards the model across (--tp N). No default is stated, so set it per model to the number of cards the weights need.

--max-num-seqs.label: Max sequences per step
--max-num-seqs.why: The largest number of sequences one step may carry. Required for Radiance: Forge refuses to launch without it. It bounds the KV cache together with the context length, so it is a per-model choice with no default.

--max-model-len.label: Max context length
--max-model-len.why: Context bound in tokens. 0 means the model's training context, which is rarely what you want, so always set it explicitly per model. It reserves nothing per request; with the sequence count it sizes the KV pool.

--kv-cache-dtype.label: KV cache dtype
--kv-cache-dtype.why: Storage type of the KV cache. Radiance 2.x takes bf16, i8 or fp8 and refuses the packed types; Radiance 1.x takes bf16, fp8, fp8_v4 or k6_v4, not i8. The smaller types cost fewer bytes per token of context at some loss of precision; choose per model.

--num-speculative-tokens.label: Speculation depth
--num-speculative-tokens.why: Speculative window: how many draft tokens each step tries. 0 disables speculation. The default is auto (the drafter's own operating point), so set it explicitly per model. A model with no draft head is unaffected.

--kernels.label: Kernel libraries
--kernels.why: The kernel libraries Radiance loads, separated by ',' or ':'; the first that matches wins and unnamed ones are not loaded. Without it every library on the search path is used (the host may set RADIANCE_KERNELS in the build's launch environment).
